conflicts: ground-state hyperfine constants: King & Jaccarino 1954 (uncorrected) 79Br A = 884.810(3), B = -384.878(8) MHz; 81Br A = 953.770(3), B = -321.516(8) MHz versus Brown & King 1966 with second-order correction (Chichinin Table 2) 884.809774(62), -384.882835(200); 953.768180(62), -321.524277(200). The B values differ by more than the 1954 error bar because of the second-order correction.
2P1/2 lifetime: measured 0.96(9) s (He et al. 1999) versus 1.11 s from the NIST A = 0.90 s^-1 and 0.90 s calculated; all compatible within the experimental error except NIST's rounded A (1.6 sigma).

5s resonance lines 157.6, 154.1, 148.8, 163.3, 157.5 nm: the oscillator strengths of Clyne & Townsend 1974 (abstract: f = 1.16(8)e-3, 4.88(59)e-2, 4.13(39)e-2, 6.4(1.2)e-3, 1.5(5)e-2, i.e. A = 2.1e6, 1.37e8, 1.24e8, 8.0e6, 2.0e7 s^-1) are 1.0 to 2.9 times smaller than the values NIST adopts from Tellinghuisen & Clyne 1976 (5.7e6, 2.2e8, 2.0e8, 2.3e7, 2.0e7 s^-1), who re-analysed the same absorption data with the hyperfine structure included. The 1976 values are kept as the entry, the 1974 ones as alternatives.
not_found: radiative lifetime of 5p 4D°3/2 (76743.08 cm^-1, the 260.6 nm / 844.9 nm scheme) and of all other 5s, 5p, 6p levels in levels.csv: no measurement located in an openable source (Lawrence 1967 states that Br lifetimes could not be measured and gives calculated A values only).

Faraday Trans. 2 72, 783 (1976) are still closed (RSC full text 403, no Wayback copy of the PDF; only the abstract, without numbers, was read); the A values entered are those NIST adopted from it. isotope shift 79Br-81Br: Cowley & Wahlgren (arXiv:astro-ph/0512294) mention that a shift of about 2.5 mA was measured for Br I 6122 A by Tolansky (Proc. R. Soc. A 136, 585 (1932)); no sign or uncertainty given, not entered.
notes: Literature search was limited: the session's web-search quota was exhausted, so sources were located through Crossref, HAL, OSTI, arXiv and NASA ADS queries and only open copies could be read. Ground-term hyperfine constants are second-hand from Chichinin's JPCRD review (method 'compilation'); the King & Jaccarino 1954 numbers were read on the APS abstract page. B < 0 for both isotopes as printed. The M1 A value is the calculated one adopted by NIST. Two-photon entries: wavelength_vac_nm is the laser wavelength. Second pass (2026-10-01): the measured lifetime of the TALIF upper level was found in the abstract reproduced by OSTI/INIS (ETDEWEB record 22362940). Third pass (2026-10-02): added the five 4p5 2P - 5s vacuum-ultraviolet resonance lines with measured A values. NIST's transition-probability reference T3064 for these lines was checked to be Tellinghuisen & Clyne 1976, the hyperfine-corrected re-analysis of the Clyne & Townsend 1974 absorption measurements; the uncorrected 1974 oscillator strengths (read in the abstract on the archived RSC page) are kept as alternatives, converted to A (derived). Morton 2000 (saved as pdf/Br_Morton_2000.pdf) states that the 1976 paper corrected the 1974 one.
